settings.httpCaptureExposedWarning: Bound to {{host}}: anything that can reach this address can use RedLog as an open proxy, and its traffic lands in your evidence. Only do this on a network you control.
settings.browserNotFound: No Chromium-based browser found — set a path above
settings.displayZoneHint: Every event time in the app is printed in this zone, and a UTC time ends in Z. Exports stay ISO 8601 with the offset.
settings.agents.selfExclusionHint: A `.redlog-app-root` file in a repo opts it out of tailing — commit one to keep RedLog out of that repo.
settings.engagementIdHint: Generated when the project was created, stamped on every event, not editable. Include it in a bug report.
settings.engagementNameHint: Display only. Changing this renames the project — the title bar and the project picker follow.
settings.operatorIdHint: Stamped on every event as who did it. Events already recorded keep the old ID.
settings.operatorNameHint: Display only — the timeline and the bundle signature. It does not affect attribution.
settings.name: Name
settings.whitelist: Safe IPs — where it's OK to attack from (VPN/VPS exits). External IP matching → SAFE (green).
settings.blacklist: Exposed IPs — your own fixed IPs (home ISP, office). External IP matching → EXPOSED (red, identity leak).
settings.ipModeHint: DNS is quieter but can be blocked; Auto tries DNS, then HTTP.
settings.showWifiNameHint: macOS asks for Location Services once so the HUD can show the real SSID. Location data never leaves this machine.
settings.pollingOpsecHint: Every poll is an outbound third-party request. At 10s that is ~8,600 a day — a beacon a defender can fingerprint. Use 60s+ or your own endpoint.
settings.confirmations: Readings required before the address changes
settings.confirmationsHint: CGNAT or load-balanced egress can answer differently each poll; requiring identical reads stops the badge flickering.
settings.ipProvidersHint: Tried in order until one answers. Must return JSON with an "ip" field.
settings.vpnAdaptersHint: Adapter names that count as a VPN tunnel. Presets can be toggled; custom patterns are case-insensitive regex.
settings.overlayAutoShow: Open the HUD when a project starts
settings.overlayAutoShowHint: When off, open the HUD from the status bar or the menu bar icon.
settings.overlayShowMark: Show Mark button in the expanded overlay
settings.overlayPassThroughHint: Clicks pass through to the window below and the HUD dims. Exit with ⌘⇧P or the menu bar.
settings.clipboardEnableHint: When a credential or token is copied, stores only its SHA-256, length, line count and matched types. Raw text never lands; detected credentials get their own loot event.
settings.clipboardStorePreviewHint: Stores a redacted 120-character preview beside the hash. Leave off if redaction gaps are a concern.
settings.fileWatcherEnableHint: Emits file_transfer when watched files change. Built-in ignores: node_modules/, .git/, dist/, out/, build/, .DS_Store and editor temp files.
settings.fileWatcherIgnoreHint: Gitignore-style globs on top of the built-in defaults. One per line.
settings.processMonitorEnableHint: Emits process_spawn and process_exit for new processes. Windows is unsupported; RedLog's own processes are ignored.
settings.processMonitorIgnoreHint: Match by leading token (first word or basename). Case-sensitive.
settings.overlayShowInDockHint: Off hides the Dock icon while the HUD is open; run it from the menu bar.
settings.rotationHint: Per-store size budget in MB; 0 = keep everything. Over budget, the coldest out-of-scope files are evicted first and in-scope targets are pinned. Events and SHA-256 always survive.
settings.retentionLoggedTier: Traffic events (HTTP / DNS / process) keep days
settings.retentionLoggedTierHint: Days to keep logged-tier rows (HTTP flows, DNS, process spawn). 0 = keep forever. These rows are not hash-chained; they serve as investigative context.

plugins.sample.masked: As it would be masked ({{count}} spans):

plugins.apiAhead: Targets a newer plugin API than this RedLog. Only the parts it understands are read; anything newer is ignored.
plugins.consentTitle: Trust this plugin to run code inside RedLog?
plugins.consentBody: "{{name}}" ships code that RedLog will load into its own main process. It is not isolated: it can read and write anything RedLog can — the evidence log, signing keys and hash chain included — and it runs with your account's access to files, network, and shell. Only trust plugins whose source you trust.
plugins.consentWarn: Trust is pinned to the plugin's current code. If the code changes, trust is revoked until you review it again.
timeline.detail.ioOnDisk: output recorded — {{size}} of session capture, expand below to read it
timeline.detail.ioUnbracketed: output not bracketed — RedLog could not match this command to a span of the session recording. Try the full session replay below.
timeline.detail.ioNotCaptured: output not captured — external shells record the command only. Prefix with `redlog-run` to capture stdout/stderr, or use the built-in terminal.
capture.rogueWhy: Switching it off in RedLog does not stop it — it runs in your own shell. The teardown is under External capture sources, in Settings ▸ Other capture sources.
capture.auditHint: Every source, including the ones switched off, never installed, or brought by a plugin — for answering whether anything is recording that you did not put there.
capture.dbGaps: {{count}} write failure(s) this session, first at {{since}} — the record has gaps
capture.unattributedSpool: {{count}} temp file(s) from shell commands typed while no project was open ({{range}}). They are not part of any project's record.
capture.unattributedSpoolWhere: Kept as *.unattributed files in ~/.redlog/pending — no project could claim them. Dates are file write times.
capture.unattributedClearMessage: These are commands typed while no project was open. No project's record has them, and once the files are deleted they cannot be recovered.
capture.unattributedClearKeeps: The open project's record is not changed.
capture.unattributedClearGone: Only the files from {{range}} are deleted; anything set aside after that stays.
capture.unattributedClearAck: I understand these cannot be recovered

overlay.keepOpenOffHint: Auto-collapses after 8s of inactivity. Click to keep it expanded.

timeline.detail.httpBodyBinary: response body not captured — {{size}} of {{type}}, which is not a textual type.

settings.wsl.networkNat: Networking: NAT — localhost unreachable from WSL
settings.wsl.networkNotConfigured: Networking: not configured — WSL may not reach localhost
settings.wsl.stopped: Distro stopped — start it to manage hooks
settings.wsl.hookInstallFailed: Could not install the hook in {{distro}}
settings.wsl.hookInstallFailedWhy: The distro answered, but writing the shell profile did not succeed. It may be read-only, or another process holds it.
settings.wsl.hookUninstallFailed: Could not remove the hook from {{distro}}
settings.wsl.hookUninstallFailedWhy: The distro answered, but editing the shell profile did not succeed. The hook is still active.
settings.wsl.distroUnreachableWhy: The distro did not respond. It may be stopped — start it from Windows, then try again.
toast.exportFailedWhy: Nothing was written. The destination may be unwritable, or the export was cancelled.
browser.failedWhy: The browser binary could not be started. Check the path and proxy in Settings ▸ {{page}}.
screenshots.deleteFailed: Could not delete the image file
screenshots.deleteFailedWhy: The event stays in the chain either way — only the JPEG was going to be removed.
capture.actionFailedWhy: The hook was not changed. The shell profile may be read-only, or the path no longer exists.
transcript.copyFailedWhy: The clipboard refused the write. Another application may be holding it.
project.openMissingWhy: The folder is gone or on a volume that is not mounted.
confirm.ackDefault: I understand this cannot be undone.
settings.cdpNotConnectedTitle: Chrome is not answering on the debugging port
settings.hookFailedWhy: The shell profile was not written. It may be read-only, or the path in Settings no longer exists.
plugins.grantFailedWhy: The plugin stays unable to run. The reason is below.
settings.anchorFailedWhy: Events keep being chained, but nothing timestamps them externally until an anchor lands. Check network access and retry.
settings.integrityNoAnchorsWhy: There is nothing to anchor yet — the chain is empty.
project.openFailedWhy: Nothing was changed or loaded. The database may be locked by another RedLog window.
project.leaveMessage: This recording stops. Everything already written stays in the project, and reopening it carries on from there.
project.leaveMessageCounted: This recording stops. The {{count}} events already written stay in the project, and reopening it carries on from there.
project.leaveNoCapture: Nothing is recorded until a project is open again — commands, HTTP traffic and screenshots in between go nowhere.
project.leaveTerminals: {{count}} terminal panes and their running jobs stay open. Their recordings end here and resume in the next project.
terminal.tabClosedWhy: The shell process ended. Undo opens a new one — scrollback does not come back.
toast.recordingPausedWhy: Capture sources stop feeding the timeline. Your markers and RedLog’s own audit events keep recording.
plugins.disabledWhy: Saved now, for every project. It does not remove shell hooks or stop tools that are already sending events.
plugins.globalNote: Switches here apply to every project on this computer. Each project's own capture sources are set under {{page}}.
plugins.loadFailed: The plugin list could not be loaded. This does not mean there are none.
plugins.failedWhy: Nothing was changed. The list below is what RedLog read back.
targets.addedToScopeWhy: Not written yet — undo within 8 seconds and nothing reaches the audit log.
targets.addToScopeFailedWhy: Another project is open or the settings could not be saved. Nothing was changed.
settings.hookRemovedWhy: Not written yet — undo within 8 seconds and the profile is never touched.
issues.scopeUnsetDetail: Until targets are declared, nothing is marked in or out of scope — including anything already recorded.
issues.scopeUnknown: Scope state could not be read
issues.scopeUnknownDetail: RedLog cannot tell whether a target is in scope, so nothing is shown as in scope while this lasts.
issues.integrity.sample-broken: A row failed its own verification
issues.integrityDetail: Handed over now, this record would not verify. Chain verification has the detail.
issues.captureDetail: Events are still being written, but at least one source has stopped producing — the gap will be in the timeline, not in an error.
issues.chainBroken: The evidence chain does not verify
issues.chainBrokenDetail: A row between the anchor and now does not hash to its successor. Export a bundle before doing anything else.
issues.chainAnchorMismatchDetail: Every row hashes to its successor, but the chain no longer matches its latest anchor: it was rewritten or cut short after it was anchored. Export a bundle before doing anything else.
fatal.title: {{view}} stopped working
fatal.why: Nothing has been lost — events already recorded are on disk and the chain is intact. Only this view stopped rendering.
fatal.scrubbed: Paths are reduced to the app bundle, and your username and project name are replaced. Read it before sending — this is exactly what gets shared.

confirm.deleteProjectChain: Every event and the whole SHA-256 evidence chain
confirm.deleteProjectMedia: All screenshots and terminal session recordings
confirm.deleteProjectAnchors: The OpenTimestamps receipts — these cannot be regenerated, because they attest to a moment that has passed
screenshots.emptyReason: Nothing has been captured yet, by hand or on a timer; periodic capture is off by default. Every screenshot carries a SHA-256 and the reason it was taken.
loot.emptyReason: Credentials and keys are detected in command output and clipboard content as they go past. Nothing has matched yet — which is the expected state at the start of an engagement.
targets.emptyReason: Hosts and addresses are extracted from commands, HTTP traffic and DNS queries as they are captured. Nothing has been seen yet — run something against a host and it will appear.
bookmarks.emptyReason: Bookmarks are your own browsing notes — the URL and title of the tab you are on, saved so you can come back to it. They are not evidence: not chained, not signed, editable, deletable, and not in the evidence bundle. For a finding that belongs in the record, drop a marker (⌘⇧M).
transcript.emptyReason: This is what you typed and what came back, in order. It fills from shell commands, agent turns and HTTP exchanges as they are captured.

firstRun.title: Get this engagement fully recorded
firstRun.hint: Two core captures, each verified by something that actually arrives. Do them in either order.
firstRun.stuckTitle: A command ran, but nothing arrived
firstRun.stuckWhy: python3 and curl are both installed, but no command has arrived. Check the capture sources below for what is quiet.
firstRun.installManually: install it with your package manager
firstRun.missingTitle: Commands here are not being recorded
firstRun.policy.title: PowerShell will not load your profile
firstRun.policy.why: This machine's execution policy is {{policy}}: $PROFILE is a script, so it is never loaded — RedLog's hook line is in it and will never run, and not one command from your own PowerShell reaches the Timeline.
firstRun.policy.builtinOk: The built-in terminal is unaffected (it starts with -ExecutionPolicy Bypass). One pane recording while the other is silent is this policy, not a broken machine.
firstRun.policy.fix: Allow local scripts for this user only:
firstRun.record.reasonPolicy: The execution policy is {{policy}}, so $PROFILE is not loaded. Run this first: {{command}}
firstRun.missingWhy: The capture hook needs {{names}}, which is not installed. Commands still run, but nothing is recorded until it is.
firstRun.record.blocked: {{shell}} can't be recorded yet — install this first. Nothing has been changed.
firstRun.record.scope: Your terminal records the command, exit code, duration and working directory — not the output.
firstRun.record.scopeBash: Bash records the command, exit code, duration and working directory, and automatically saves ordinary command output. Interactive programs may record commands only; use session recording for a full interactive record.
firstRun.record.sessionHint: Need the output too? Run this in that terminal first; everything after it is recorded:
firstRun.record.paste: Open a new terminal tab and paste:
firstRun.record.waiting: Waiting for that command to arrive…
firstRun.record.timeoutTitle: Nothing arrived in 60 seconds. The most likely reasons:
firstRun.record.reasonNewTab: The shell profile was not loaded. Tabs that were already open don't pick up the hook — open a new tab and paste the command there.
firstRun.record.reasonMissing: {{names}} is missing, so the hook cannot send anything:
firstRun.http.title: HTTP(S)
firstRun.http.manualInstall: Install manually, then return here to retry
firstRun.http.needsPrereq: mitmproxy installs with {{command}}, which isn't on this machine. Install {{command}} first, then check again.
firstRun.http.timeoutTitle: No HTTP request in 60 s. Most likely:
firstRun.http.reason.paused: Recording is paused, so a check cannot pass: nothing is being recorded. Resume recording (status bar), then run a new check.
firstRun.http.reason.browser: Your usual browser does not use this proxy — set it as in step 1, or use “Check in the capture browser”.
firstRun.http.reason.ca: The HTTPS certificate is missing or not trusted, so HTTPS sites cannot pass the proxy — see “HTTPS certificate” below.
firstRun.http.reason.terminalsOff: curl and wget in your terminals do not use the proxy — “route new terminals through this proxy” is off by default.
firstRun.http.reason.terminalsNew: Only built-in terminals opened after turning the option on use the proxy; ones already open do not.
firstRun.http.proxyLead: 1. Point your browser at this proxy (HTTP and HTTPS):
firstRun.http.proxyHint: Enter it in the browser's proxy settings, or a switcher extension such as FoxyProxy. RedLog never changes your system proxy.
firstRun.http.caDownload: 2. Trust the CA below. In a browser that already uses this proxy, http://mitm.it also serves it for download.
firstRun.http.verifyOwn: 3. Check in your own browser: open this address once it uses the proxy and trusts the CA.
marker.readonly.urlWhy: where the mark points; changing it changes what it points at
loot.noMatchesReason: The type filter or de-duplication is hiding every hit. Nothing was removed from the record.

settings.hookDesc.codex: Wraps the Codex shell so the agent's commands are captured

settings.hookDesc.shell-powershell: Captures commands from PowerShell via a prompt hook

eventTitle.connectionSaturated: ⇄ {{count}} connections in one poll — recording the count, not each
filter.title: Filter
filter.unappliedTitle: {{condition}} is not applied on this page
filter.unappliedHttpType: HTTP History only holds the HTTP traffic the proxy recorded, so its source type is fixed. The selected type has nothing to show here, which is why the list is empty — that is not evidence the project recorded no HTTP traffic or no events of that type.
filter.unappliedTranscriptType: The Transcript only buckets these source types: {{types}}. The selected type is not one of them, so this page has nothing to show — that does not mean the project holds no events of that type.
filter.chainedOnlyHint: Show chained evidence only, the tier that is hashed and signed. Applies to every event view.
filter.chainedOnlyHttp: HTTP flows are recorded in the logged tier, so Chained only leaves nothing here. That is not evidence the project recorded no HTTP traffic.
filter.lootTypeEmpty: Loot lists only loot rows, so {{condition}} leaves nothing here. That is not evidence the project holds no events of that type.
filter.inScopeHint: Show only events targeting in-scope hosts
filter.personalHiddenHint: Hides event rows whose target matches your personal/local rules. Untargeted events and terminal recording contents are not classified. Click to show matching rows.
filter.personalShownHint: Showing rows matching your personal/local target rules. Click to hide those rows.
marker.replayAtTime.noSession: No active terminal session at this time
terminal.castTruncated: Cast recording hit size limit — output past this point is not captured
terminal.castPaused: Recording paused — this pane's output is not written while paused
terminal.castNotRecording: No cast recording for this session
query.tokenCondition: Condition: matched against the stored field
query.unparsable.empty-condition-value: “{{token}}” is a half-typed condition with no value. Give it one, or wrap it in double quotes to search for it as text.
transcript.queryToolSessionOthers: The same tool-use ID also occurs in {{count}} other session(s); add a session: condition to choose.
transcript.queryCoverage: Text search covers stored event content. Command output that was not captured inline stays in a terminal recording and cannot be matched — no hit is not evidence the output never held it.
palette.searchFailed: Event search failed — this is not the same as no matching events.
palette.searchUnparsable: That condition is incomplete (e.g. nothing after session:), so no search was run. Add a value, or quote it to search it as text.
palette.searchSubset: Newest {{count}} matches — Search lists all of them

settings.lootRulesFailed: Could not load the loot rules.
statusBar.uptimeSince: Time since this project was created ({{date}}), not this session
settings.lootRuleStopped: Stopped: this rule ran past its time limit, so it no longer runs — or masks what it matches. Reload the plugin after fixing the pattern.
settings.externalCaptureHint: These need root or change this machine, so you run the command. Applies to every project on this machine.

capture.core.heading: Core capture
firstRun.http.rejected: ✗ a client refused RedLog’s certificate — it does not trust the CA
firstRun.http.captureBrowserCaveat: RedLog’s capture browser ignores certificate errors, so this does not show that other tools trust the CA.
firstRun.http.verifyFromTool: Or check the tool you will actually use:
firstRun.http.verifyNoInsecure: No -k / --insecure: HTTPS passes only if this tool trusts RedLog’s CA. Turning certificate checks off would prove nothing.
firstRun.http.reason.caRejected: A client refused RedLog’s certificate: it does not trust the CA yet — see “HTTPS certificate” below.
httpCapture.caTrustStores: Each tool has its own proxy setting and its own trust store: curl and wget read the system store; Python requests uses certifi (REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE); Node needs NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS; Java uses its keystore; Firefox keeps its own. Trust it where each tool looks — do not switch certificate checks off.
settings.packMemberOptIn: Off by default — turning the pack on does not turn this on.
app.closeSaveFailed: A settings change could not be saved to this project, so it was not closed. Check the settings and try again.
settings.loadFailedWhy: The project’s configuration did not load, so nothing here can be shown or changed yet.
